audit_status.source_base: Greek Jude text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Complete one-chapter draft reviewed for contending for trust, false teachers, wilderness/angel/Sodom warnings, Michael tradition, Enoch citation, mercy, doxology. Relation to 2 Peter and non-canonical citations require second-pass audit.

verses.restored: Jude, servant of Jesus Messiah and sibling of James, to those called, beloved in Divine Father and kept for Jesus Messiah:

familiar.text: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called:

modern.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James, To those who are called, loved by God the Father, and kept in Jesus Christ:

original.text: Ἰούδας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος, ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἰακώβου, τοῖς ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ ⸀ἠγαπημένοις καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ τετηρημένοις κλητοῖς·

verses.restored: Mercy to you and peace and love be multiplied.

familiar.text: Mercy unto you, and peace, and love, be multiplied.

modern.text: Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you. God’s Judgment on the Ungodly (2 Peter 3:1–7)

original.text: ἔλεος ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ ἀγάπη πληθυνθείη.

verses.restored: Beloved, making all eagerness to write to you concerning our common salvation/healing, I had necessity to write appealing to you to contend for the trust once handed over to the holy ones.

familiar.text: Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.

modern.text: Beloved, although I made every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I felt it necessary to write and urge you to contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints.

original.text: Ἀγαπητοί, πᾶσαν σπουδὴν ποιούμενος γράφειν ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς κοινῆς ⸀ἡμῶν σωτηρίας ἀνάγκην ἔσχον γράψαι ὑμῖν παρακαλῶν ἐπαγωνίζεσθαι τῇ ἅπαξ παραδοθείσῃ τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστει.

verses.restored: For certain humans slipped in unnoticed, those long ago written beforehand for this judgment, irreverent ones turning the grace of our Divine into licentiousness and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

modern.text: For certain men have crept in among you unnoticed—ungodly ones who were designated long ago for condemnation. They turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality, and they deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.

original.text: παρεισέδυσαν γάρ τινες ἄνθρωποι, οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τὸ κρίμα, ἀσεβεῖς, τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριτα μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον ⸀δεσπότην καὶ κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἀρνούμενοι.

verses.restored: Now I wish to remind you, though you know all, that the Lord, having saved/healed a people out of Egypt, afterward destroyed those not trusting.

familiar.text: I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.

modern.text: Although you are fully aware of this, I want to remind you that after Jesus had delivered His people out of the land of Egypt, He destroyed those who did not believe.

original.text: Ὑπομνῆσαι δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, εἰδότας ⸂ὑμᾶς ἅπαξ⸃ ⸀πάντα, ὅτι ⸀Ἰησοῦς λαὸν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου σώσας τὸ δεύτερον τοὺς μὴ πιστεύσαντας ἀπώλεσεν,

verses.restored: And messengers who did not keep their own beginning/office but left their own dwelling, he has kept in age-long bonds under gloom for judgment of great day.

familiar.text: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.

modern.text: And the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling—these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.

original.text: ἀγγέλους τε τοὺς μὴ τηρήσαντας τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν ἀλλὰ ἀπολιπόντας τὸ ἴδιον οἰκητήριον εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρηκεν·

verses.restored: As Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities, in like manner giving themselves over to sexual immorality/misuse and going after other flesh, are set forth as example, undergoing justice of age-long fire.

familiar.text: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

modern.text: In like manner, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, who indulged in sexual immorality and pursued strange flesh, are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.

original.text: ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γόμορρα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις, τὸν ὅμοιον ⸂τρόπον τούτοις⸃ ἐκπορνεύσασαι καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, πρόκεινται δεῖγμα πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι.

verses.restored: Yet likewise these dreamers also defile flesh, reject lordship, and blaspheme glories.

familiar.text: Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.

modern.text: Yet in the same way these dreamers defile their bodies, reject authority, and slander glorious beings.

original.text: Ὁμοίως μέντοι καὶ οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσιν, κυριότητα δὲ ἀθετοῦσιν, δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσιν.

verses.restored: But Michael the archangel, when disputing with the adversarial one, was reasoning about the body of Moses, did not dare bring blasphemous judgment, but said: May Lord rebuke you.

familiar.text: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.

modern.text: But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Μιχαὴλ ὁ ἀρχάγγελος, ὅτε τῷ διαβόλῳ διακρινόμενος διελέγετο περὶ τοῦ Μωϋσέως σώματος, οὐκ ἐτόλμησεν κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν βλασφημίας, ἀλλὰ εἶπεν· Ἐπιτιμήσαι σοι κύριος.

verses.restored: But these blaspheme what they do not know; and what they understand naturally like irrational living creatures, by these they are corrupted.

familiar.text: But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.

modern.text: These men, however, slander what they do not understand, and like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.

original.text: οὗτοι δὲ ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασιν βλασφημοῦσιν, ὅσα δὲ φυσικῶς ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ἐπίστανται, ἐν τούτοις φθείρονται.

verses.restored: Woe to them, because they went in the way of Cain, and poured themselves into the error of Balaam for wages, and perished in the rebellion of Korah.

familiar.text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

modern.text: Woe to them! They have traveled the path of Cain; they have rushed headlong into the error of Balaam; they have perished in Korah’s rebellion.

original.text: οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Κάϊν ἐπορεύθησαν, καὶ τῇ πλάνῃ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ μισθοῦ ἐξεχύθησαν, καὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ Κόρε ἀπώλοντο.

verses.restored: These are hidden reefs in your love-feasts, feasting with you fearlessly, shepherding themselves, waterless clouds carried along by winds, autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted,

familiar.text: These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;

modern.text: These men are hidden reefs in your love feasts, shamelessly feasting with you but shepherding only themselves. They are clouds without water, carried along by the wind; fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted.

original.text: οὗτοί εἰσιν ⸀οἱ ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες συνευωχούμενοι, ἀφόβως ἑαυτοὺς ποιμαίνοντες, νεφέλαι ἄνυδροι ὑπὸ ἀνέμων παραφερόμεναι, δένδρα φθινοπωρινὰ ἄκαρπα δὶς ἀποθανόντα ἐκριζωθέντα,

verses.restored: wild waves of sea foaming up their own shames, wandering stars, for whom gloom of darkness has been kept into the age.

familiar.text: Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.

modern.text: They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom blackest darkness has been reserved forever.

original.text: κύματα ἄγρια θαλάσσης ἐπαφρίζοντα τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας, ἀστέρες πλανῆται οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους εἰς αἰῶνα τετήρηται.

verses.restored: And Enoch, seventh from Adam, also prophesied to these, saying: Look, Lord came with his holy myriads,

familiar.text: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints,

modern.text: Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them: “Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones

original.text: Προεφήτευσεν δὲ καὶ τούτοις ἕβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ Ἑνὼχ λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν κύριος ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: to make judgment concerning all and to expose every soul/life concerning all their works of irreverence that they irreverently did, and concerning all the hard things that irreverent sinners/misaligned ones spoke against him.

familiar.text: To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

modern.text: to execute judgment on everyone, and to convict all the ungodly of every ungodly act of wickedness and every harsh word spoken against Him by ungodly sinners.”

original.text: ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων καὶ ἐλέγξαι ⸂πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς⸃ περὶ πάντων τῶν ἔργων ἀσεβείας αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατʼ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς.

verses.restored: These are grumblers, fault-finders, going according to their desires, and their mouth speaks swollen things, admiring faces for advantage.

familiar.text: These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.

modern.text: These men are discontented grumblers, following after their own lusts; their mouths spew arrogance; they flatter others for their own advantage. A Call to Persevere (Hebrews 10:19–39; 2 Peter 3:1–7)

original.text: οὗτοί εἰσιν γογγυσταί, μεμψίμοιροι, κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας ⸀αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα, θαυμάζοντες πρόσωπα ὠφελείας χάριν.

verses.restored: But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Messiah,

familiar.text: But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ;

modern.text: But you, beloved, remember what was foretold by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ

original.text: Ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀγαπητοί, μνήσθητε τῶν ῥημάτων τῶν προειρημένων ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

verses.restored: that they were saying to you: In last time there will be mockers going according to their own irreverent desires.

familiar.text: How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts.

modern.text: when they said to you, “In the last times there will be scoffers who will follow after their own ungodly desires.”

original.text: ὅτι ἔλεγον ⸀ὑμῖν· ⸂Ἐπʼ ἐσχάτου χρόνου⸃ ἔσονται ἐμπαῖκται κατὰ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἐπιθυμίας πορευόμενοι τῶν ἀσεβειῶν.

verses.restored: These are the ones making divisions, soul-level, not having Spirit.

familiar.text: These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.

modern.text: These are the ones who cause divisions, who are worldly and devoid of the Spirit.

original.text: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀποδιορίζοντες, ψυχικοί, πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες.

verses.restored: But you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy trust, praying in holy Spirit,

familiar.text: But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost,

modern.text: But you, beloved, by building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit,

original.text: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀγαπητοί, ⸂ἐποικοδομοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς τῇ ἁγιωτάτῃ ὑμῶν πίστει⸃, ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ προσευχόμενοι,

verses.restored: keep yourselves in love of Divine, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Messiah into age-long life.

familiar.text: Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.

modern.text: keep yourselves in the love of God as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you eternal life.

original.text: ἑαυτοὺς ἐν ἀγάπῃ θεοῦ τηρήσατε προσδεχόμενοι τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

verses.restored: And have mercy on those doubting,

familiar.text: And of some have compassion, making a difference:

modern.text: And indeed, have mercy on those who doubt;

original.text: καὶ οὓς μὲν ⸀ἐλεᾶτε ⸂διακρινομένους,

verses.restored: save/heal others by snatching from fire; and on others have mercy with reverent caution, hating even the garment stained by flesh.

familiar.text: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.

modern.text: save others by snatching them from the fire; and to still others show mercy tempered with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh. Doxology (Romans 16:25–27)

original.text: οὓς δὲ σῴζετε ἐκ πυρὸς ἁρπάζοντες, οὓς δὲ ἐλεᾶτε ἐν φόβῳ⸃, μισοῦντες καὶ τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐσπιλωμένον χιτῶνα.

verses.restored: Now to the One able to guard you unstumbling and to stand you before his glory blameless in exultation,

familiar.text: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,

modern.text: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy—

original.text: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ φυλάξαι ⸀ὑμᾶς ἀπταίστους καὶ στῆσαι κατενώπιον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἀμώμους ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει

verses.restored: to only Divine our Savior/Healer through Jesus Messiah our Lord be glory, majesty, strength, and authority before all the age and now and into all the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.

modern.text: to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity. Amen.

original.text: ⸀μόνῳ θεῷ σωτῆρι ἡμῶν ⸂διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν⸃ ⸀δόξα μεγαλωσύνη κράτος καὶ ἐξουσία ⸂πρὸ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος⸃ καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.

safety_note: Jude contains severe polemic and apocalyptic imagery. Do not use it to dehumanize opponents, demonize ordinary disagreement, or target vulnerable groups. The polemic addresses exploitative, divisive, self-serving teachers who distort grace and harm the community. Sodom/Gomorrah and 'other flesh' require second-pass source and reception-history audit to avoid later prooftext misuse.
translation_notes: Jude uses traditions also known from 1 Enoch and the Assumption/Testament of Moses stream; non-canonical citation metadata required in second pass.
Mercy remains central in vv. 21-23 even amid severe warnings.
Doxology centers the Divine's ability to guard from stumbling.
